meta.label: Hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars
meta.source: EPA and DOE fueleconomy.gov; NHTSA 5-Star Safety Ratings; Science Based Targets initiative
meta.attribution: Every full hybrid and plug-in hybrid the EPA rated for model year 2026 or 2027, one row per make, nameplate and powertrain (model year 2026 where it exists), from the EPA and DOE vehicle file on fueleconomy.gov: 45 hybrids and 29 plug-in hybrids. Mild hybrids, whose engine description in the file says "Mild Hybrid" and which the EPA lists as hybrids, are left out here and kept on the new cars list. 21 plug-in nameplates the EPA rated for model year 2025 have no 2026 or 2027 rating in this file, among them the Toyota RAV4 and Toyota Prius plug-in hybrids. The file does not say which have ended and which are not yet rated, and none is on this list until the EPA rates it. Running cost is the EPA's yearly fuel or electricity cost for the median configuration, for 15,000 miles with 55 per cent city driving at the fuel prices fueleconomy.gov used (at $4.47 a gallon of regular and 15 cents a kilowatt-hour in this file), scored as a share of the cheapest on this list. For a plug-in hybrid it is fueleconomy.gov's combined electricity and gasoline figure, which assumes the share of miles on electricity the EPA sets for that car; each note also gives its cost on gasoline alone. Crash ratings are NHTSA's overall stars, joined only to the model NHTSA names with the same year, make and powertrain, and scored on the lowest-rated tested version; a model NHTSA has not tested is left unscored. NHTSA advises comparing frontal crash ratings only between vehicles within 250 pounds of each other. The maker's climate target is SBTi's record for the company whose EPA manufacturer code certifies the vehicle, matched by LEI; a maker SBTi does not list is left unscored, not marked down. Purchase prices are not in these registers and are not scored.
